synopses.large:
Celebrating a modern comedy classic. It’s the 20th anniversary of Not Going Out, the sitcom created, written and starring the brilliant Lee Mack. In this very special half-hour documentary, he invites us to hear the inside story of how the series came to be and why it’s stood the test of time.

It’s the longest-running British sitcom still in production, and there is exclusive access behind closed studio doors to see exactly how the show is made. From the initial spark in a writers’ meeting, through theatre read-throughs where, uniquely, scripts are tested on an audience to intensive rehearsals and finally the studio recording, cameras follow Lee, the cast and crew as they bring together a brand new series coinciding with the show’s milestone birthday.

In an in-depth interview, Lee shares the story of the show from his own perspective, with plenty of fascinating details and funny anecdotes along the way. Fellow stars Sally Bretton, Tim Vine, Hugh Dennis, Abigail Cruttenden, Deborah Grant and Geoffrey Whitehead reflect on its phenomenal success, alongside guest stars Chris McCausland and Jocelyn Jee Esien, as well as producer Jamie Rix and director Nick Wood. Classic clips and rarely seen footage add extra context, insight and, of course, lots of laughs.

synopses.small: BBC Wales’s Lucy Owen celebrates Welsh news and entertainment from the year 2000.
synopses.medium: News from the noughties. What was Wales talking about at the turn of the millennium? Lucy Owen looks back at serious and silly stories from the BBC archives.

synopses.large:
Lucy Owen explores BBC Wales’s archives of 2009, with gems that include the BBC Wales presenters in a Strictly dance-off for Children in Need. 

The wild Kashmir goats of Llandudno provide a new regimental mascot for the Royal Welsh. Boffins in Aberystwyth wonder if elephant grass could provide a new biofuel, and we observe Harry Potter’s shell house in Pembrokeshire. 

The Institute of Astronomy donates a giant telescope to Knighton, and the best private collection of Welsh quilts goes on public show. There’s a skunk on the loose in Tredegar, and the women’s tug o’ war team train for the World Championships.
synopses.small: BBC Wales presenters take part in a Strictly dance-off for Children in Need.
synopses.medium: Lucy Owen takes a personal trip through the BBC Wales news and entertainment archives of 2009, including BBC Wales presenters taking part in a Strictly dance-off for Children in Need.
